archetype: BG -1/-1 aristocrats. Hapatra converts other cards' -1/-1 counters into deathtouch bodies, and the bodies convert into cards and drain. deck-audit reads the frame's archetype as combo and applies the combo overrides (protection 4-6, tutors 4-8); the frame's own words are 'a converter engine, not a combo deck', and the measured rates agree with the frame — the median engine assembles at 67.2% while the two named kills sit at 16.3% and 9.5%.
verdict: The deck functions and converts. Its mana is the best thing about it (36 lands, zero taplands, 90.2% on the turn-3 land drop, commander plus a payoff at 67.2%), and its median plan — mint Snakes, feed a drain converter — is genuinely redundant. What limits it is not a count anywhere near the engine: it is interaction-breadth, measured at 1 class of 5, and an enumeration of all 88 entries confirms rather than softens it. No card in the 99 destroys or exiles an artifact, an enchantment or a land, and exactly one touches an opponent's graveyard. Two other flagged axes are artifacts of the taxonomy and are named as such below.

engine.declared: Hapatra mints a 1/1 deathtouch Snake every time you put one or more -1/-1 counters on a creature; the Snakes feed a free sacrifice outlet; a drain converter turns each death into life loss.

components.reading: The at-will, mana-free, repeatable -1/-1 sources, enumerated from every card in the 99 whose text contains '-1/-1', 'wither' or 'blight'. Only Yawgmoth is unbounded and it needs fodder; Devoted Druid can only counter itself and dies on its third activation (its second without Mikaeus); Serrated Arrows has exactly three arrowheads and then sacrifices itself. The four other repeatable sources — Hapatra herself, Blowfly Infestation, Obelisk Spider, Necroskitter — are all gated on combat damage or on a death. goldfish_targets.json does not declare this class, so no simulation has ever priced it.
Six deep and the deck's most reliable target: commander plus any payoff assembles 67.2% of games at mean turn 3.62. This is the half that is not scarce.

Any drain converter, 51.9% assembled at mean turn 3.34. Note only two of the four hit every seat: Zulaport Cutthroat and Bastion of Remembrance say 'each opponent loses 1 life'. Blood Artist drains a single target player per death and Blasting Station pings one target per activation.

Five free sacrifice outlets, an adequate class on its own. But all five are named in checker-passed stack 001's step 10 as outlets that place no -1/-1 counter, so each yields exactly one extra undying return under Mikaeus, not a loop. The 9.5% figure prices an assembly the verified stack says does not loop.

One copy, 7.1% of an opening seven. Its verified value in this list is Devoted Druid (a true two-card infinite of deaths, counters and Snakes, explicitly not of mana) and Walking Ballista plus any free outlet (a three-card kill) — neither of which the declared target names.
One copy carrying the deck's headline two-card kill at 16.3%. It has never been through a stack scenario, so it is a plausible line, not a fact.
The deepest component in the deck, and the reason a three-card enabler class is playable at all. 78.0% of games see one, 67.6% by turn 6.

single_points_of_failure.why: Everything downstream of Hapatra is a function of counter placements, and the class that supplies them at will without mana is three cards: Yawgmoth, Devoted Druid and Serrated Arrows. Two of the three are self-bounded — Devoted Druid can only place counters on itself, Serrated Arrows has exactly three activations. The corpus prices a 5-card class at 31% of openers; this one is smaller than that and is not even declared to the simulation. The pool cannot close it as defined. Of the 43 cards in candidate_pool.json whose oracle text places a -1/-1 counter, the mana-free at-will activations outside the three already in the 99 are Grim Poppet (enters with exactly three counters, at {7}), Cinderhaze Wretch (places counters on itself only, and its 3/2 body dies to the second, at {4}{B}) and Fume Spitter (sacrifices itself) — each reproducing the exact defect that disqualifies Devoted Druid or Serrated Arrows. Carnifex Demon charges {B} per activation and holds two counters. The closers below therefore meet weaker properties, and not the same one as each other. Sinister Gnarlbark and Persistent Constrictor are free, unbounded and repeat every turn, but on a fixed trigger rather than at will: Gnarlbark blights at your end step and draws a card; Constrictor blights at each opponent's upkeep, so three placements a turn cycle, gated on an opposing creature. Glistening Oil is weaker still and is not unbounded — it enchants one creature and places counters only on that creature, so a single casting yields at most that creature's toughness in placements, and each re-attachment after the Aura returns to your hand costs {B}{B} again; price it as the bounded, recastable member. The relaxation is real and worth naming: at-will matters for holding up a response and for a single-turn kill; free-per-turn still multiplies Snakes every turn. Harbinger of Night is excluded: its upkeep trigger is symmetric and puts a counter on each creature, which sweeps the 1/1 Snakes and Insects the payoff half is built on.

cut_candidates.why: Two mana for a single -1/-1 counter — one Snake, once — attached to a proliferate that costs {4} and a tap. It is a cuttable slot rather than the cheapest one: interaction sits at 14 copies against a floor of 8, so the axis can afford to lose a copy, and this is the copy whose loss costs no body and no free placement. The other thin slot on that named 14, Fume Spitter, is a {B} body Yawgmoth eats for a card and it places its counter for free, so it stays.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: One ETB counter placement (so one Snake, or an Insect with Nest of Scarabs out), and one of the deck's two repeatable proliferate effects — the 99 holds exactly three proliferate cards, Grim Affliction (a one-shot instant), Contagion Clasp and Yawgmoth's {B}{B} discard. That costs more than the interaction count suggests: proliferate gives 'another counter of each kind already there', so Contagion Clasp is the only repeatable non-Yawgmoth way to put an arrowhead counter back on Serrated Arrows — one of the three cards in the ignition class, the engine's thinnest component. Grim Affliction can do it once.

cut_candidates.why: Upkeep-only, one target a turn, and the trigger is mandatory: with a legal target it must be put on the stack, and this deck routinely leaves -1/-1 counters on its own creatures — Devoted Druid holds them by design, and Yawgmoth's target keeps one. Its removal job is redundant with Yawgmoth, which does the same thing at instant speed and draws a card.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: The only card in the 99 that destroys a creature by targeting it — Mikaeus's destroy trigger is conditional and untargeted — and therefore the deck's one clean answer to a creature whose toughness is out of reach of a single counter. Toxic Deluge, Black Sun's Zenith, Walking Ballista and Yawgmoth all still scale to a large body.

cut_candidates.why: A mandatory +1/+1 counter engine inside a -1/-1 deck. Every green creature entering — every Snake, every Elf Warrior from Flourishing Defenses — forces a +1/+1 counter onto a target, and a +1/+1 counter either annihilates a -1/-1 counter this deck placed on purpose or lifts one of its own 1/1 tokens out of range of a single counter, which is what Blowfly chains need. Its payoff is Scurry Oak, and that pairing has never had a stack scenario.
cut_candidates.cost_of_cutting: Real and worth stating plainly: Ivy Lane Denizen appears in 10 of the deck's 32 deduped contained combo lines, including Scurry Oak + Ivy Lane Denizen, which bracket-check names as the highest-bracket line present. Scurry Oak keeps its other +1/+1 sources — its own evolve, Host of the Hereafter's counter transfer, Mikaeus's undying return, and every proliferate effect the deck still holds (Grim Affliction, Yawgmoth's {B}{B} ability) once it already carries one counter, since proliferate gives 'another counter of each kind already there'. Three Yawgmoth + Scurry Oak + drain lines, with Zulaport Cutthroat, Blood Artist and Bastion of Remembrance, survive the cut untouched. The bracket floor does not move — bracket-check shows game_changers forcing 4 on its own with 11 Game Changers — but the deck's combo census gets smaller and more honest.

What it does buy is a Snake every turn for zero mana (an Insect too under Nest of Scarabs, an Elf Warrior under Flourishing Defenses, a drain under Obelisk Spider), plus a card every turn; the card-advantage axis reads 8 against a target of 10, though this diagnosis reads that count as understated by the taxonomy rather than binding, so the draw is a bonus and not the case for the card. The verified Mikaeus lines are Mikaeus + Devoted Druid and Mikaeus + Walking Ballista + any free outlet. A target for the at-will free -1/-1 source class (Yawgmoth, Devoted Druid, Serrated Arrows) should be declared at the same time.
open_questions.why_it_matters: 9.5% is currently the deck's stated odds on an assembly a verified artifact says does not loop, and the class that actually gates the engine has no measured rate at all.

open_questions.question: Does Hapatra + Blowfly Infestation actually loop, and can it be stopped short of a draw? The chain needs a seed -1/-1 counter and a token that dies to one counter, and Blowfly's placement is mandatory with a chosen target.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the deck's headline kill and the better-rated of the two two-card kills goldfish tracks (16.3% against the Mikaeus target's 9.5%), and it has never been verified.

open_questions.question: Does Mikaeus's anthem switch the Blowfly and Hapatra token loops off? Snakes, Insects and Elf Warriors are non-Human, so under Mikaeus they are 2/2 and a single -1/-1 counter no longer kills them.
open_questions.why_it_matters: If it holds, the deck's two flagship engines cannot share a battlefield, which changes both the tutor order and whether Mikaeus belongs in the 99 at all.

open_questions.question: Verify Scurry Oak + Ivy Lane Denizen, and audit the six Ivy Lane entries paired with a sacrifice outlet — on the named pair alone none of those outlets causes a green creature to enter, so Ivy Lane never triggers.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The painful cut above rests on that pairing being unverified, and bracket-check names it as the highest-bracket line present.

open_questions.question: Is Yawgmoth + Hapatra (no Mikaeus) the deck's real kill? Sacrifice a Snake, place the counter on a body that survives it, Hapatra replaces the Snake — flat board, one card drawn, one life paid, one death trigger per activation.
open_questions.why_it_matters: It needs neither of the two cards the deck's declared targets are built around, and if it works the mulligan and tutor priorities change.

gaps: candidate_pool.json excludes lands by construction, so the cheapest fixes for the two classes this deck cannot answer are invisible to every evidence channel this deck has. Bojuka Bog (exile an opponent's graveyard on ETB) and Boseiju, Who Endures (channel to destroy an artifact, enchantment or nonbasic land) are both Commander-legal, inside B/G identity and absent from the 99; they would close breadth from a land slot rather than a spell slot. Neither appears among candidate_pool.json's 229 listed candidates or in any of upgrade-facts' three channels for this deck, so neither can be cited as a pool candidate here.

No deck_recon.json exists for this deck (deck-audit freshness reports recon absent), so nothing in this diagnosis is grounded in what other Hapatra lists actually run. Inclusion rates would settle whether three answers is the norm or whether this list is an outlier.

strategy.md has no aristocrats or sacrifice-engine section and no counters-matter section. The outlet / fodder / converter taxonomy, the difference between a free and a costed outlet, and the +1/+1-versus--1/-1 annihilation tension that motivates the Ivy Lane Denizen cut were all derived from oracle text and stack 001, not from the corpus. research-strategy is the route.

The at-will free -1/-1 source class has no hypergeometric figure anywhere in the artifacts because goldfish_targets.json does not declare it. The 31%-at-5-copies line from strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors is the nearest published anchor and it is for a different class size.

No card in candidate_pool.json meets the ignition component's full definition (at-will, mana-free, repeatable, unbounded, any target). That is an enumeration over the 43 pool cards whose oracle text places a -1/-1 counter, not a search of the whole format — the pool is built from owned and shortlisted cards and excludes lands, so a format-wide answer may exist and would not appear here. deck-recon is the route.

findings.note: The superlative fails on oracle text against the deck's own artifacts. The entry says 'Blowfly is the only card in the 99 whose -1/-1 placement chains off another creature's death'. Host of the Hereafter is in the 99: 'Whenever this creature or another creature you control dies, if it had counters on it, put its counters on up to one target creature you control' — trigger on another creature's death, effect a -1/-1 counter placement, structurally the same conditional as Blowfly's own 'if it had a -1/-1 counter on it'. It is not a marginal reading: bracket_report.json's two_card_infinites list (the same list axes[15] takes its '19 two-card infinites' from, reproduced by a fresh `bracket-check`) carries {'bracket':1, 'cards':['Hapatra, Vizier of Poisons','Host of the Hereafter'], 'produces':['Infinite LTB','Infinite ETB','Infinite death triggers']} — the census pairs it with the commander exactly as it pairs Blowfly. The cause is the probe method the diagnosis states for itself in engine.components[0]: 'enumerated from every card in the 99 whose text contains -1/-1, wither or blight'. Host of the Hereafter's oracle text contains '+1/+1' and 'counters' but not '-1/-1', so the probe cannot see it, and the entry reads the probe's floor as a ceiling — which is the exact failure deck-audit's own notes block warns about ('An axis count is a floor'). The doctor read the card: cut_candidates[2] cites 'Host of the Hereafter's counter transfer' as a +1/+1 source for Scurry Oak. Consequences the entry then states as fact: 'closers: []' and 'none of candidate_pool.json's 229 listed candidates repeats that pattern' (the 229 count I reproduced exactly) present Blowfly as a chain with no partner anywhere, when a same-function partner is already sleeved and paired with the commander in the deck's own combo census. I am NOT asserting the Hapatra + Host line loops — no stack has run it — and the superlative fails on oracle text alone, before that question arises.

The sentence 'The verified Mikaeus lines are Mikaeus + Devoted Druid and Mikaeus + Walking Ballista + any free outlet' is a closed enumeration, and stack 001 (checker.verdict == pass, 4 iterations) establishes a third that it omits. Step 12: 'Yawgmoth, Thran Physician is one of the deck's EIGHT mana-free sacrifice outlets and the only one that is also a repeatable reset', 'That counter annihilates an undying +1/+1 counter under 704.5q, so this outlet does not hit the step-10 wall', resolving to 'a FOUR-CARD assembly — Mikaeus + Yawgmoth + two non-Human creatures — collapsing to three cards plus the commander's Snakes when Hapatra is on the battlefield', 'A strong engine, not a true infinite' because it is library-bounded. The checker's own clean-pass finding lists 'the A/B Yawgmoth loop and its library bound' among the conclusions it independently re-derived, so this is checker-passed, not an aside. The omission is load-bearing because this open question is the instruction to re-declare goldfish_targets.json: handed this list, goldfish would re-declare Mikaeus targets that again exclude the single outlet in the deck that beats the step-10 wall. The same gap sits under engine.components[3]'s 'Five free sacrifice outlets' and engine.single_points_of_failure[1]'s 'all five members ... are named in checker-passed stack 001', both of which quote step 10's conclusion while step 10's own census — 'FULL OUTLET CENSUS, since my earlier counts were wrong twice: eight of this deck's sacrifice outlets have no mana in their activation cost' and 'Exactly one of the eight — Yawgmoth — also places a -1/-1 counter' — says the class is eight and names the exception in the sentence after the one quoted.

ADJUDICATING THE ARITHMETIC THE ORCHESTRATOR RAISED: considered and dismissed, not missed. It is NOT a defect. The deck is 88 entries / 100 copies (deck-audit counts, reproduced); 3 cuts and 2 adds applied together would leave 99 copies, i.e. a 98-card deck plus commander. But nothing in the contract makes these lists a mandated swap set that must balance. .claude/skills/diagnose-deck/SKILL.md:18-19 states 'Analysis-only. Nothing in this loop edits decklist.txt or cards.json. Applying a swap is a separate, human act.' The deck-doctor charter describes them as ranked lists and makes `natural_cut` — the per-add pairing — optional; validate_diagnosis.py enforces only that a natural_cut is a real maindeck card, not the commander, and not double-claimed. It nowhere compares len(cuts) to len(adds), and it passes this document. The document's own prescription IS balanced and IS one-for-one: add_candidates[0] Assassin's Trophy -> natural_cut Crumbling Ashes (= cut_candidates[1]), add_candidates[1] Sinister Gnarlbark -> natural_cut Ivy Lane Denizen (= cut_candidates[2]), both distinct singleton maindeck entries, so the prescribed swaps hold the deck at 88 entries / 100 copies. cut_candidates[0] Contagion Clasp is offered unpaired, which is what a candidate list is for. Requiring the two lists to balance would import a contract the artifact does not have and would penalise offering a cut candidate the doctor did not want to pair. Separately on this block: the charter's 'A cut list with no painful entry is a list that dodged the job' is satisfied — Ivy Lane Denizen is `painful` and argued at length, the other two are `contested` and neither is a disguised `easy`. orphans_stack is [] on all three and correct: stack 001's scenario board is Hapatra / Mikaeus / Ashnod's Altar / Blood Artist / one Snake token, and none of the three cut cards appears in it.

The liability verdict and the verdict block's claim behind it are the strongest-supported things in the document, and I re-derived the enumeration rather than accepting it. Pulling oracle text for all 88 entries from cards.csv and grepping destroy|exile returns exactly two destroy effects in the 99 — Crumbling Ashes ('At the beginning of your upkeep, destroy target creature with a -1/-1 counter on it') and Mikaeus ('Whenever a Human deals damage to you, destroy it') — and no card destroys or exiles an artifact, an enchantment or a land, as the verdict states. The only card touching an opponent's graveyard is Abstergo Entertainment, and the reading describes it correctly: '{3}, {T}, Exile Abstergo Entertainment: Return up to one target historic card from your graveyard to your hand, then exile all graveyards' — self-exiling, and it takes your own graveyard with theirs. '88 entries' matches deck-audit counts.entries exactly. I also reproduced the metric itself by importing deck_audit._interaction_breadth with card_roles.json: base = {creature: 14}, one class.

Every countable claim checks out and the enumeration is exhaustive as stated.
